why: Intro to the terminal plan (docs/ui-next/catalog/plans/intro-terminal.json), 'Variables, arguments and a loop' (passes: ./count.sh rain prints one line for each note with its count). The script is right, but the learner ran `./count.sh` with no word. $1 is empty, and `grep -ci ""` matches every line, so each note prints 3 (its line count). With rain the counts are 2, 1 and 1. A line per note with a number is on screen, but not the rain counts the step asks for.

step.title: Count a word in every note
step.instructions: Write count.sh: it takes a word as $1 and, for each file in notes, prints the file name and how many lines mention the word (grep -ci). Make it executable with chmod +x count.sh, then run ./count.sh rain.

checks.label: ./count.sh prints a count for each note

files.trail-log/notes/day1.txt:
Woke to rain on the tent
Afternoon rain, trail muddy
Camp by the river
files.trail-log/notes/day2.txt:
Light rain
Sun by noon
Saw a heron
files.trail-log/notes/summit.txt:
Reached the summit
Rain cloud below us
Cold wind
files.trail-log/count.sh:
#!/bin/zsh
word=$1
for f in notes/*.txt; do
  echo "$f: $(grep -ci "$word" "$f")"
done
